title: Rav Yehudah the Indian
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a convert, as stated explicitly in Kiddushin 22b: Rav Yehudah the Indian (Rashi explains: from the land of Kush; the Arukh explains: from the land of Havilah) was a convert without heirs. He fell ill; Mar Zutra went to visit him, saw that he was dying, and acquired his slave. In Bava Batra 74b they said: “Rav Yehudah the Indian related: Once we were traveling on a ship, and we saw a precious stone around which a sea-serpent was coiled,” etc. See also the entry Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah.

notes.text: The source’s הינדואת in the Bava Batra 74b quotation is read as הינדואה. Saved Davidson Bava Batra 74b has הינדוא. The old reader note incorrectly called this Bava Kamma; its original remains archived. Rashi’s Kush and the Arukh’s Havilah interpretations stay attributed, distinct from the English epithet Indian.
